instruction:
Read the git restore reference without running commands. Explain the default restore destination and default content source when neither --staged nor --source is supplied. Then explain what --staged changes and which source is used by default with that option. State how the reference says to target both the index and the working tree. Cite the DESCRIPTION and OPTIONS sections and give the documentation version shown.

Stopping condition: Stop when the destination/source defaults, the effect of --staged and the way to target both destinations are explained with versioned documentation citations.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Identify that the default restore destination is the working tree when neither --staged nor --source is supplied. Full credit if explicitly stated, or if the agent attempts to access the documentation but clearly reports that the website is inaccessible/down.

Identify that the default content source is the index when neither --staged nor --source is supplied. Full credit if explicitly stated, or if the agent clearly reports that the documentation website is inaccessible/down.

items.criterion: Explain the effect of --staged and its default source
items.description: Identify that the --staged option changes (restores) the index, and that its default source is HEAD. Full credit if both are stated, or if the agent reports the site is inaccessible. Partial credit (1 point) if only one is stated.

items.criterion: State how to target both the index and the working tree
items.description: Explain that both destinations can be targeted simultaneously by using both --staged and --worktree options. Full credit if stated, or if the agent clearly reports that the documentation website is inaccessible/down.

items.criterion: Cite the DESCRIPTION and OPTIONS sections
items.description: Include citations from the DESCRIPTION and OPTIONS sections of the documentation to support the answers. Full credit if both sections are cited with the documentation source URL(s), or if the agent reports the site is inaccessible. Partial credit (1 point) if only one section is cited.

Report the git documentation version shown on the page during the run. Full credit if the version number matches the documentation shown during the run, or if the agent clearly reports that the documentation website is inaccessible/down.
